@graph.name: Automating this takes no developer

step.name: Send the account guides over

step.name: We load and provision

step.name: Orders begin arriving finished
step.text: Spoken, approved and delivered by your chosen route. Most buyers send one the day they are set up.

@graph.name: Which parts does distribution automation software like this cover?

acceptedAnswer.text: One stretch, end to end: a customer deciding what they need, the order being written up and approved, and the result landing in your systems coded, with its own reference. Everything after that, from picking to delivery to the invoice, belongs to the software you have.

@graph.name: Will it place orders for our customers automatically?

acceptedAnswer.text: No, and that is a design decision rather than a missing feature. A person reads the lines and sends them. Nothing goes out on a customer's behalf, because an order sent by a machine on a bad assumption is a credit note with extra steps.

@graph.name: Can we really get rid of the retyping?

acceptedAnswer.text: On the EDI, QuickBooks and API routes, yes: the record arrives in your system without anyone touching it. If you take orders as an emailed PDF, Excel or Word file instead, somebody may still key it in. That is the one choice in setting up distribution automation software worth thinking about properly.

@graph.name: Do we need middleware or a developer?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. There is nothing to host, no script to write and no integration platform in the middle. We agree the delivery method with you during onboarding and it keeps working without maintenance.

@graph.name: Can the old way keep running alongside it?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Phone orders still get handled by a person, exactly as now, and they carry no reference or send time from us. The place to begin is your most frequent orderers, since that is where the hours pile up.

@graph.name: Is this automated software distribution, as in deploying software?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. If you are looking for an automated software distribution tool to push applications and patches out to laptops and servers, that is a different field entirely. VOS has no part in it. We are about food orders moving from a restaurant to its distributor.

@graph.name: Does this relate to grid distribution automation?

acceptedAnswer.text: Also no. In the electricity industry the same term covers feeder switching, fault location and outage management on a power network. Nothing here touches utilities. The overlap is only in the words.

@graph.name: How many accounts need to move for this to be worth doing?

acceptedAnswer.text: Savings land per order, not per customer, so it turns on how often they order. Start with the handful of customers ordering most often. We quote for each distributor, so ask us to run through the arithmetic on the call.
